facts.text: The fever and chills started 5 days ago.
My skin and the whites of my eyes have turned yellow.
Three months ago I had my gallbladder removed by keyhole surgery.
The gallstones caused an infection of the bile ducts, cholangitis, and that's why my gallbladder was taken out.

aliases: red cell breakdown disorder in the family
facts.text: Nobody in my family has a disease where the red blood cells break down.

findings.name: liver function tests
findings.result: Total bilirubin 10.9 mg/dL (direct 6.0 mg/dL); AST 49 IU/L; ALT 65 IU/L; ALP 441 IU/L; GGT 301 IU/L.

findings.name: abdominal contrast CT
findings.result: Splenomegaly; distended left kidney; no biliary-tract obstruction.

findings.name: urinalysis
findings.result: Leukocyte esterase 3+, nitrite 2+, hemoglobin 3+, bilirubin 2+, urobilinogen 3+; sediment: white cells, bacteria, and 5–9 erythrocytes per high-power field.

findings.name: Coombs tests
findings.result: Direct and indirect Coombs tests negative.

gold.reasoning: 1. Acute obstructive suppurative cholangitis was considered because of fever, jaundice, and elevated liver‐function tests, but it was excluded because “no signs of biliary tract obstruction were present.” 2. Pyelonephritis was suggested by the urine findings and imaging, as “urinalysis findings suggested the diagnosis of septicemia due to pyelonephritis; however, the cause of the patient’s hyperbilirubinemia was unclear.” 3. Other infections accompanied with hyperbilirubinemia, such as infectious mononucleosis, malaria, and Weil syndrome (leptospirosis), were deemed unlikely because “other infections … were unlikely in light of negative findings of the microbiological examination and peripheral blood smear.” 4. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia was excluded because “the results of direct and indirect Coombs tests were negative.” 5. Hereditary spherocytosis was strongly suspected on the basis of “peripheral blood smear findings, splenomegaly and the patient’s past history of cholelithiasis.”

Ethnicity (Asian) is a social-background fact, not part of demographics.
The cholecystectomy three months earlier and its reason (gallstones causing cholangitis) are medical-history facts.
